title: User ask sprint lanes — customer feedback clusters (May 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Collect and synthesize customer feedback gathered during Apr–May outreach (N = ~32 enterprise conversations + support tickets). Goal is to translate buyer asks into sprintable lanes for the next two product sprints and surface low-friction fixes we can ship in 1–2 weeks. This is intentionally tactical (not an exhaustive VOC report).

Context and collection notes:
- Sources: discovery calls, renewal conversations, support backlog tags (billing, performance, private-deploy), ad-hoc field interviews by AE/SEs.
- Sampling bias: heavy enterprise / platform-team representation; fewer single-team startups.
- Signals weighted qualitatively by frequency, revenue impact, and operational risk reported by customers.

Top clusters (high-level) and representative asks:
1) Latency predictability for tail requests (hosted API and Dedicated)
   - Common phrasing: "We need consistent 95th/99th percentiles — bursts kill SLAs."
   - Top asks: predictable token latency under burst; more transparent routing rules; ability to pin region+capacity for low tail latency.
   - Frequency: 18/32 conversations flagged as medium-high pain.
   - Severity: High for customers with latency SLOs (ad apps, realtime chat).
   - Proposed quick wins:
     * Expose current routing policy for a model on the Console (read-only): who/which policy is routing to which tier/region. Owner: Console PM. ETA: 1 sprint.
     * Add a sampling trace for 95/99p token latency to the per-route dashboard (basic visualization + explanation). Owner: Observability eng. ETA: 2 weeks (minimal).
   - Mid-scope: Canary a pinned-region deployment UI for Dedicated customers (requires backend routing + UI). Owner: Dedicated product. ETA: 2–3 sprints.

2) Cost controls for high-throughput embedding & reranking workloads
   - Common phrasing: "We love the throughput but per-token costs are unpredictable when usage spikes or when model variants change."
   - Top asks: rate-limited batching knobs, per-route quantization profiles, clearer per-call cost estimates in API response headers.
   - Frequency: 12/32 flagged; especially large customers running daily embedding pipelines.
   - Severity: Medium-high (directly impacts monthly invoices).
   - Proposed quick wins:
     * Add optional response headers with estimated token-cost and model-variant ID. Owner: API infra. ETA: 2 weeks.
     * Document recommended batching settings for common throughput patterns (1‑page playbook). Owner: DevRel. ETA: 1 week.
   - Mid-scope: Per-route cost guardrails (hard budget caps and soft throttles) in Console. Owner: Product (Optimize). ETA: 3–4 sprints.

3) Private deployment on-boarding friction (VPC & on-prem)
   - Common phrasing: "The private install works, but SSO/KMS and audit logs are painful to wire up — takes weeks."
   - Top asks: clearer network diagrams, pre-flight validator for customer infra, sample KMS bindings, packaged audit-forwarding config.
   - Frequency: 9/32 flagged (larger regulated customers).
   - Severity: High for deals in pipeline (several renewals contingent on faster onboarding).
   - Proposed quick wins:
     * Publish a one-click preflight checklist and small script (curl-based) that validates basic VPC/KMS connectivity. Owner: Private deployments eng. ETA: 1 sprint.
     * Ship updated onboarding template for solutions engineers (checklist + common gotchas). Owner: Solutions Eng. ETA: 1 week.
   - Mid-scope: A lightweight deployment wizard in Console (guided steps for VPC/KMS/audit). Owner: Private product + Console. ETA: 3–4 sprints.

4) Model-compat fallbacks and graceful degradation paths
   - Common phrasing: "When a primary model is out, we need automatic fallback without quality cliffs or format changes."
   - Top asks: model variant chaining, automated output-schema compatibility checks, configurable fallback policies per route.
   - Frequency: 7/32 flagged.
   - Severity: Medium (product stability).
   - Proposed quick wins:
     * Add route-level toggle: allow_fallback_to_compatible_variants (boolean) with documentation. Owner: API product. ETA: 2 weeks.
     * Small docs + example configs for canonical fallback chains used by top customers. Owner: DevRel. ETA: 1 week.

Proposed sprint lanes (prioritized):
- Lane A (1 sprint): Observability & transparency small-bets
  - Expose routing policy, 95/99p latency sampling, cost-estimate response header. (Owners: Console PM, Observability, API infra)\  - Value: unblock ~40% of flagged customers.
- Lane B (1 sprint): Private-deploy onboarding artifacts
  - Preflight validator script + SE onboarding template. (Owners: Private eng, Solutions Eng)
- Lane C (2–3 sprints): Cost guardrails + per-route quantization profiles (Optimize)
- Lane D (2–3 sprints): Pinned-region/Dedicated UI for latency-sensitive customers

Representative customer snippets (anonymized):
- "Our shortest path to launch is reducing tail latency — sometimes a single spike spikes our whole flow and we miss user SLAs." — large fintech platform
- "We can't afford surprises on the monthly invoice; if quantization flips or model changes, costs ballooned last month without us understanding why." — adtech scale-up
- "The private install itself is OK but getting KMS and audit logs plumbed took our infra team 3 weeks; we almost lost the renewal." — healthcare customer

Open/unknowns and risks:
- We need engineering input on whether adding cost estimates in headers is reliable today (depends on runtime token-counter accuracy for in-flight batching). Action: ENG TPM to validate (jira:ENG-7890).
- Routing policy visibility could leak internal placement details if not carefully filtered. Security review required.
- Preflight validator script must avoid exposing keys/creds and must be idempotent; legal/infosec sign-off needed for distribution.

Immediate asks for Product/Eng teams (this week):
1) Observability: quick feasibility check on adding 95/99p token sampling to per-route dashboards (estimate dev effort in story points). (owner: Observability Eng lead)
2) API infra: confirm feasibility and safety of token-cost estimate header for batched requests (can we present an estimate that is within +/- X%?). (owner: API infra lead)
3) Private eng + Solutions Eng: agree on minimal preflight checklist and assign a reviewer. (owner: Private eng PM)

Next steps and timeline:
- By EOD next Tuesday: product owners to confirm lane ownership and feasibility notes (observability, API infra, private deploys).
- Next 2 sprints: ship Lane A and Lane B (target: two small deliverables per lane).
- End of sprint 2: revisit with updated customer signals (renewal motions) and reprioritize Lane C/D if revenue-impacting requests rise.

Appendix: quick dataset counts used for synthesis:
- Total conversations: ~32
- Mentions: latency predictability (18), cost controls (12), private onboarding (9), fallback/compat (7) — items can overlap (customers raised multiple asks).

Notes to self / field heuristics (informal):
- When customers ask for "predictable latency" they usually mean tail-percentiles and region affinity. Don’t assume they mean average latency.
- Small docs + shipped headers/visibility go a long way; many customers prefer a small telemetry leak rather than a major UI feature.
- Prioritize quick SE artifacts (playbooks, scripts) — low dev cost, high perceived value.

Action owners (proposed):
- Console PM: expose routing policy (read-only)
- Observability Eng: latency sampling + dashboard tile
- API Infra: cost-estimate header + fallback toggle
- Private Eng: preflight validator script
- Solutions Eng: onboarding template + SE playbook

Questions for CS leadership:
- Do we want to proactively contact the subset of customers who raised onboarding risk and offer a "fast track" private deployment (SE hours)?
- Any objections to shipping a 'best-effort' cost header as a beta feature to selected customers?

-- end --
